points.t: Recurrent painful **‘boils’ in the same flexural sites**, with **double comedones**, tunnels or rope-like scars.
Follicular **occlusion and rupture**, then IL-17 / TNF inflammation; obesity, smoking, genetics add risk.
Weight and smoking support, antiseptic washes, analgesia; **topical clindamycin** (mild); **tetracycline course**; early referral.
**Under-treatment and delay**: tunnels and scars are irreversible. Also depression, and **SCC** in long-standing perianal disease.

cause.lead: Blocked follicles that rupture deep in the skin.
points: Follicular **occlusion → rupture →** innate immune cascade → **tunnels** and fibrosis.
Drivers: genetics (~⅓ family history), obesity / friction, **smoking**, hormones, dysbiosis.
Women ≈ 3:1 in Western cohorts; onset after puberty.
**Follicular occlusion triad**: HS, acne conglobata, dissecting cellulitis of the scalp (tetrad adds pilonidal disease).
Not caused by poor hygiene; not contagious.

visuals.caption: Hurley staging in cross-section: I – abscesses without tunnels; II – recurrent abscesses with tunnels and scarring, separated by normal skin; III – diffuse interconnected tunnels and abscesses across the region.
visuals.alt: Three skin sections showing Hurley stages I to III

points: **Paired ‘tombstone’ comedones**, painful firm nodules, abscesses, **draining tunnels**, rope-like scars.
Sites: **axillae**, groin, under the breasts, buttocks, perianal / perineal, neck.
**Hurley I**: abscesses, no tunnels. **II**: recurrent with tunnels and scars. **III**: diffuse interconnected.
Once tunnels exist, Hurley stage doesn’t step down with medicines alone.

visuals.caption: Clues in the armpit: paired ‘tombstone’ comedones, deep tender nodules and rope-like scars. A boil doesn’t leave this pattern.
visuals.alt: Armpit skin with paired comedones, nodules and scars

points: Typical lesions + typical sites + **≥ 2 flares in 6 months**.
Often negative or colonised: supports a sterile picture.
Ultrasound / MRI before surgery; biopsy chronic anogenital ulcers (SCC).
Hurley stage, sites, smoking, BMI, prior antibiotics.

cards.name: Boils / carbuncles
cards.clue: Discrete pointing abscesses; no tunnels or rope scars.

cards.name: Epidermoid / Bartholin cyst
cards.clue: Single cyst; no multi-site comedonal disease.

manage.lead: Treat early; abscess drainage alone doesn’t modify disease (BAD guideline).

points: Not infectious, not ‘dirt’; validate pain and QoL.
**Stop smoking**, weight management, loose clothing, chlorhexidine washes, non-adherent dressings.
Pain: paracetamol / NSAID.
**Clindamycin 1% BD** to active lesions (short adjunct).
Tetracycline-class course (doxycycline / lymecycline), review ~12 weeks; stewardship.
Clindamycin + rifampicin (~12 weeks), steroid rescue, acitretin, dapsone, metformin / anti-androgens.
**Biologics** (adalimumab, secukinumab per NICE TAs); surgery for tunnels.

limits.t: Screen metabolic syndrome, diabetes, PCOS, CVD risk, depression.
Intent changes antibiotic, retinoid and biologic choices: ask early.

items.t: **Hurley II–III**, or failed 12-week tetracycline: dermatology for systemic or biologic therapy.
Chronic non-healing ulcer in long-standing perianal / buttock HS: exclude **SCC**.
Low mood or suicidal thoughts: high psychological burden, support and refer.

pearls.t: Third recurrence in the same fold? Stop calling it a boil: **think HS**.
Waiting lists are long: refer early, don’t wait for tunnels.
Drainage relieves pain but doesn’t change the disease.

quiz.q: Hurley stage with tunnels and scarring separated by normal skin?

quiz.a: Clindamycin 1% twice daily to active lesions.

quiz.q: Classic clue that separates HS from boils?
quiz.a: Paired (tombstone) comedones, tunnels and rope-like scars in flexures.
